headline: Entry Passes Required for the Cabot Trail Scenic Drive
reservation: A valid park pass is required for all vehicles stopping on the Cabot Trail or using park facilities; these are available at park entry gates or visitor centers in Chéticamp and Ingonish. While entry does not currently use a lottery, the park's campgrounds are highly sought after and require separate reservations through the Parks Canada system. Regulations regarding backcountry camping and group access vary, so visitors should verify current status on the official website before travel.

days.title: Acadia Coastline and Canyon Vistas

stops.name: Skyline Trail
stops.detail: Walk the dramatic headland boardwalk for expansive views of the Gulf of St. Lawrence where the mountains meet the sea.

stops.name: MacIntosh Brook
stops.detail: A gentle forest walk leads to a hidden waterfall set within an old-growth hardwood canyon.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours for the western climbs; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: The western ascent involves steep grades and sharp switchbacks near French Mountain.

days.title: Plateau Barrens and Hidden Waterfalls

stops.name: Lone Shieling
stops.detail: Explore a replica of a Scottish sheep crofter's hut nestled in one of the oldest protected forests in the Maritimes.

stops.name: Beulach Ban Falls
stops.detail: Drive into the Aspy Valley to witness one of the park's highest cascades falling from the highland plateau.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours of travel time; slow down for potential wildlife crossings.
days.note: Cellular reception is extremely limited in the Aspy Valley and interior plateau.

days.title: Atlantic Coves and Granite Cliffs

stops.name: Lakies Head
stops.detail: Observe the rugged pink granite coastline and crashing Atlantic waves from this iconic roadside viewpoint.

stops.name: Middle Head Trail
stops.detail: Hike the rocky peninsula separating North and South Ingonish Bays for views of the Keltic Lodge and distant Cape Smokey.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local exploration; road construction is common during summer months.
days.note: Expect higher traffic volumes near the Ingonish beach area and local services.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: The Skyline Trail parking lot often reaches capacity by mid-morning during peak autumn foliage season. Smaller coastal pull-offs like Lakies Head offer limited space and require careful maneuvering near the road edge.

intel.title: Topographic Interference
intel.text: Expect significant dead zones for mobile data between Pleasant Bay and Neil's Harbour. Offline maps are essential for navigating the inland plateau sections of the Cabot Trail.

intel.title: Coastal Gateway Services
intel.text: Refuel in Chéticamp or Ingonish as there are no fueling stations within the national park boundaries. Ensure your vehicle is prepared for the significant elevation changes of the North Mountain pass.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Status
intel.text: The Cabot Trail is generally accessible year-round, but park facilities and secondary roads like the one to Mary Ann Falls typically close from late October to May. Check the Parks Canada site for seasonal gate openings.

intel.title: Cycling and Grade
intel.text: Cyclists should be aware of the 13% grades on French Mountain and Mackenzie Mountain. The road features narrow shoulders in several canyon sections which may challenge those unfamiliar with mountain driving.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental at Sydney (YQY) and stock up on supplies in Sydney or North Sydney before the two-hour drive to the Ingonish entrance.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are suitable for the Cabot Trail, though RVs should check brake health for steep descents.
plan.goldenHour: Lakies Head provides a dramatic Atlantic sunrise setting, depending on seasonal cloud cover.
